title: sdks: unify auth/retries semantics across Python/TypeScript/Go; streaming ergonomics; parity & v1.45.0 bump
author: Asha Patel
description:
Context: Multiple SDKs (python/typescript/go) had subtle behavioral differences in how auth token refresh, retry backoff, and streaming APIs behaved under transient failures. This caused parity issues in integrations, confusing ergonomics for streaming handlers, and a handful of production incidents where clients silently dropped streams or retried in tight loops.

This PR unifies the public surface and semantics across the three SDKs: standardized auth refresh hooks, common retry policy configuration and defaults (exponential backoff + jitter, capped retries), and a new ergonomic streaming API surface that normalizes error propagation and cancelation behavior. It also includes parity fixes found during cross-language QA and bumps package versions to v1.45.0.

What changed (high level): consolidated auth token refresh interface, central retry middleware shared design, streaming API refactor to expose an "on_message"/"on_error" callback set and an async iterator wrapper for languages that support it, parity fixes for TypeScript and Go around header propagation and reconnect logic, test additions and CI matrix expansion.

Migration notes: Default retry behavior changed slightly (more conservative retry limit but smarter backoff). Existing users with custom retry configs are unaffected; users relying on prior implicit streaming behavior should migrate to the explicit streaming handler pattern documented in the changelog.

Testing: unit tests added for auth refresh race windows, integration tests for streaming reconnect semantics, cross-language e2e parity tests were run in the CI matrix. Benchmarks show negligible overhead in the hot path and improved stability under flakey network conditions.

Follow-ups: polish docs and samples in separate PRs, consider opt-in legacy behavior for a deprecation window if customers need the old streaming semantics.
